notes: All four raw texts were re-fetched from their URLs into rev-LA/raw. The Catholic Encyclopedia vol. 3, Hamilton 1901 and Aritonang & Steenbrink 2008 copies are byte-identical to the drafter's raw files. Every quote was found verbatim: the CE 'China' quote, Hamilton, both Aritonang quotes, and the three Lettres édifiantes quotes (no raw_file, so the checker marks them unchecked; I found them in the re-fetched lettresdifiantes03jesu_djvu.txt). The Periodical Accounts quote is at file line 7259. (a) CE 'China' (1908): the sentence sits in the K'ang-hi section and goes on 'the question of rites ... did not impair their credit during the reign of K'ang-hi'. It supports 'in contact with' between Chinese Catholicism and the Society of Jesus inside both rows' dates. Hamilton supports Schmidt's Moravian mission at the Cape (see MA-m1 for a quote that names Herrnhut). Each link has a primary witness plus a public-domain secondary read online, so Widely Accepted is the most allowed for the Chinese link, whose primary is also a raw online text. The Moravian link does have a Library primary checked verified-direct (Periodical Accounts 1790, line 7259). That quote is the Moravians' own account of their own Cape mission, and the earlier slice review held it at Inferential-Thin as not carrying the tie to AF-5's other churches. Open-Gaps 185 asks for Widely Accepted, and going to Documented would be a regrade beyond the ruling, so Widely Accepted is right here. Neither secondary is contested. 'A Catholic study of 1908' for an encyclopedia article is loose; 'A Catholic reference work of 1908' would be exact, but this is not a finding. (b) Aritonang ch. 9 ('rehabilitation of the life of the church as a consequence of ... the moral bankruptcy of the VOC') and ch. 6 ('the Church of the Moluccas was revitalised') carry continuity of the same church after 1815. 'Continued as' at Widely Accepted with the 1815-1861 gap named follows the coordinator's ruling on Open-Gaps 191 exactly. AP5's continuesAs, relations line and living basis match the link, and the validator's living rules are satisfied (living true, own grade 'none', descentConfidence with a basis). The relations line's two added sentences are supported. check_draft.py: no READ-FAIL, no new quote failures.
